newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's peace plan on track - minister.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's peace plan on track - minister.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government's peace plan, aimed at ending the country's 14-year ethnic war, is making progress and will yield results this year, a senior government minister said on Thursday.
Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris told a news conference in Colombo: "1996 has been, for the process of constitutional reform, a good year.
Peiris, widely believed to be the architect of the peace plan, added: "1997 is going to be a year of action, not a year of endless deliberation. Now the time has come for decisions to be made."
The peace plan, devolving wide-ranging powers to the regions and minority Hindu Tamils, is being discussed by a parliamentary select committee.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam guerrillas are fighting the predominantly Buddhist Sinhalese government for an independent homeland in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.

The proposals, unveiled by President Chandrika Kumaratunga in late 1995, need to be passed by a two-thirds majority in parliament and approved at a national referendum before they can be enshrined in the constitution.
It suggests turning Sri Lanka into a union of regions and making it a federal state in all but name.
Peiris said the select committee had 63 meetings last year, which cleared about 70 percent of the provisions of the devolution draft.
"We're determined to carry this forward and there will be finality in the very near future," he said.
He added the select committe process would be concluded in March after which "we would be able to prepare the final report of the select committee for submission to parliament".
